name: Mirror Scrivener
description:
A Mirror Scrivener is a tall, unnervingly precise construct fashioned from lacquered wood, brass hinges, and thin panes of polished silver set where a face should be. In the lantern glow of Numillian's Curated Quarter, it appears at first like a ceremonial clerk or a living statue of a scribe, but its reflection gives it away: the mirrored surface never quite matches the angle of the room, as though it is reading a second, hidden world behind the first. Its hands end in delicate quills of black metal, each fingertip capable of etching runes, sealing ledgers, or copying a witness's words with perfect, merciless accuracy.

The creature moves with quiet, measured grace, pausing often to tilt its head as if listening for discrepancies in speech, signature, or memory. When disturbed, the mirrored plates along its torso flicker with ghostly images of documents, faces, and ward-symbols, replaying fragments of what it has observed. Dust and pale motes cling to it like ash, and faint scratches mar its silver face from countless revisions. It is most often found in sealed archives, reliquaries, or gatehouse offices, where it records secrets no one intends to keep. In battle, it fights like a bureaucrat turned executioner--patient, exacting, and utterly devoted to preserving the truth it was ordered to reflect.
